Build an experimental design over an APSIM parameter space

Source: R/design.R
apsim_design.Rd

Generates parameter points filling the box [lower, upper] for the named parameters. A Latin-hypercube design (the default) spreads n points evenly through the space – the standard choice for training an emulator; a grid gives an exhaustive factorial (n becomes points-per-dimension); random gives an independent uniform sample. The design is reproducible through seed.

Usage

apsim_design(
  parm_paths,
  lower,
  upper,
  n = 20L,
  method = c("lhs", "grid", "random"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

parm_paths

Character vector of APSIM node paths (the design columns).

lower, upper

Numeric vectors of box bounds, each aligned to parm_paths (recycled from length one).

n

Integer. For method = "lhs" / "random", the number of points; for method = "grid", the number of points per dimension (so the design has n ^ length(parm_paths) rows).

method

Character: "lhs" (default), "grid" or "random".

seed

Optional integer RNG seed for the stochastic methods.

Value

A numeric matrix with length(parm_paths) named columns, one row per design point.

Examples

d <- apsim_design(c("[Sow].Script.Population", "[Fertilise].Amount"),
                  lower = c(50, 0), upper = c(200, 200), n = 8, seed = 1L)
dim(d)
#> [1] 8 2
